entries.title: How do I check my terminal arrival window and port of call schedule?
entries.text: Kriativos On Board takes place November 20–23, 2026, on MSC Musica, departing and returning to Santos with a call in Búzios. Check the day and time of the call, arrival window, and boarding instructions on your booking itinerary and voucher. Do not use the bus charter schedule as the ship's boarding time.

entries.title: Who requests cabin vouchers, when, and through which channel?
entries.text: Royal Trip manages group check-in issuance. When announced in the group chat, the cabin lead should contact Júnior privately to receive vouchers and luggage tags in PDF format. Verify passenger details and print documents. There is no guaranteed release date; follow travel agency announcements.

entries.title: Which identification document should I bring? Is digital ID accepted?
entries.text: For Brazilian citizens on this domestic route, MSC accepts RG, CNH, passport, and other recognized civil documents in good condition with a recognizable photo. Digital driver's licenses must be opened within the official government app (screenshots/copies are not accepted). Bringing physical documents is strongly recommended. Foreign travelers should bring valid passports.

entries.title: What documentation is required for minors and foreign passengers?
entries.text: Confirm specific requirements with Royal Trip based on age, accompanying guardians, nationality, and residency status. Obtain official notarized authorization forms where required in advance. Do not submit personal ID copies through public forms.

entries.title: I am pregnant: what medical clearance is required?
entries.text: MSC does not permit travel if pregnancy reaches 24 weeks at any point during the cruise. Below this limit, MSC requires an official medical certificate confirming fitness to travel and low-risk pregnancy, stating gestational age and estimated delivery date, signed and stamped by an authorized physician. Notify Royal Trip in advance.

entries.title: How do I verify baby registration and request a crib?
entries.text: All guests, including infants, must be included in the cabin booking. Minicruises permit infants under MSC regulations. Confirm fares, port taxes, crib availability, and policies with Royal Trip; do not assume automatic free admission.

entries.title: Do I need COVID-19 vaccine or test certificates?
entries.text: Check current sanitary protocols with Royal Trip and MSC closer to departure. Health regulations depend on maritime authorities and destination requirements. Always follow official guidelines issued for your specific sailing.

entries.title: What is the official MSC luggage allowance?
entries.text: Per passenger: up to two checked bags of max 23 kg (50 lbs) each (max dimensions 90 × 75 × 43 cm) and up to two carry-on pieces of max 10 kg (22 lbs) each (max dimensions 56 × 45 × 25 cm). Total luggage per cabin must not exceed 100 kg or 8 bags. Also verify separate flight or bus limits if applicable.

entries.title: How do I drop off luggage and what stays with me?
entries.text: Affix agency-issued MSC tags to all checked bags before arriving at the terminal. Keep identification, travel vouchers, medications, valuables, and essential clothing in your carry-on luggage, as checked bags are delivered to cabins later in the day.

entries.title: What items are prohibited? Are hair dryers, straighteners, or drones allowed?
entries.text: MSC prohibits weapons, illegal substances, inflammable items, and heat appliances like clothing irons. Hair dryers and hair straighteners are permitted. Drones may be brought on board if stored securely in the cabin, but flight from the ship is strictly prohibited. Commercially packaged dry snacks are generally allowed.

entries.title: What amenities does the cabin provide and what should I bring?
entries.text: Cabins include bed linens, towels, body wash, shampoo, hair dryer, TV, air conditioning, and safe. Bring personal toiletries such as toothbrush, toothpaste, and hair conditioner, plus sunscreen and compatible power plug adapters. Cabin minibars do not guarantee temperatures suitable for storing medicines.

entries.title: How does the official KOB bus charter work?
entries.text: The charter operates round-trip between Barra Funda (São Paulo) and the Port of Santos. Meeting point: Rua Tagipuru, near nº 552. Bus 1: meet 06:00, depart 06:30, tolerance 06:40. Bus 2: meet 06:40, depart 07:20, tolerance 07:30. Arrive on time; tolerance is not a second departure time. Bus 1 is confirmed. Bus 2 depends on minimum passenger threshold with full refund via Pix if not reached. Return from Santos on Nov 23 is scheduled for 10:30.

entries.title: Arriving by plane: Is there KOB airport transfer from GRU or CGH?
entries.text: The KOB charter departs strictly from Barra Funda, not from airports. Travelers flying into Guarulhos (GRU) or Congonhas (CGH) can consult regular commercial bus services (such as Viação Cometa) to Santos bus station, then take local transport to Concais. Allow generous time for holiday traffic.

entries.title: Driving by car: How does port parking work?
entries.text: Official terminal parking is operated directly by Concais in Santos with advance online reservation recommended (concais.com.br). Check rates and access guidelines directly with the terminal. Follow signage for passenger drop-off upon arrival.

entries.title: Can I access my cabin immediately after boarding?
entries.text: Cabins may still be undergoing turnover and cleaning. Readiness may be around 13:00/14:00; wait for the announcement over the ship’s public address system. Enjoy the lunch buffet while waiting and keep essentials with you.

entries.title: Is the onboard safety drill mandatory?
entries.text: Yes. International maritime safety regulations mandate that all embarking passengers complete the safety muster drill as instructed by MSC crew and in-cabin guides.

entries.title: Where and when do I pick up my welcome kit? What does it include?
entries.text: Welcome kit pickup is scheduled for 16:00/16:30 on day one at Crystal Lounge (location subject to final confirmation). The kit includes an event lanyard, wristband, collectible metal coin, and a board game tote bag from Fácil Shopping.

entries.title: Where can I find the gaming schedule and official notices?
entries.text: Look for the bulletin board at the entrance of the gaming lounge and follow the official group messaging channel. MSC's daily program also lists general ship activities.

entries.title: How do I verify lounge hours and Sunday return deadlines?
entries.text: Crystal Lounge offers open seating during daytime and evening gaming blocks. There is no promise of 24h uninterrupted gaming. On Sunday, we will announce the game return cutoff for final inventory.

entries.title: How do I register on Board Game Guru and connect with monitors?
entries.text: Board Game Guru is the official event companion app (iOS/Android). Open the KOB 2026 page and click ‘I’m going’ to enter prize raffles and view the available games library.

entries.title: I cannot use the app. Can I still participate in raffles?
entries.text: Yes. Approach the Encounter monitor desk in the gaming lounge to request manual registration on the participant list. Lack of app access will not exclude you from raffle participation.

entries.title: Can I bring personal games and prototypes, bookmark titles, and share my collection?
entries.text: Yes! Register games you bring in the Guru app (importable from Ludopedia or BGG). Favorite games you wish to play to help monitors plan tables. Mark personal games clearly and respect baggage limits.

entries.title: How do I borrow games and can I play them outside the lounge?
entries.text: Follow monitor instructions for checkout. If taking a game outside Crystal Lounge, register your name and cabin number with the desk. Please keep games in permitted relaxation areas and do not occupy dining restaurant tables for gaming.

entries.title: I booked solo or want to join a table: how do I find players?
entries.text: Ask Encounter monitors in the gaming lounge to match you with players and introduce you to games. You do not need to arrive with a pre-formed group.

entries.title: What should I wear? Is formal gala attire required?
entries.text: Bring comfortable casual clothes for daytime gaming and a light sweater for breezy decks and AC. Dinner in the main dining room is smart casual (sleeveless tank tops and flip-flops are restricted). Tuxedos or formal gala gowns are not required.

entries.title: How do I prepare for theme parties?
entries.text: The White Party (Festa do Branco) is a cruise tradition; bring white clothing if you wish to join. For KOB's Sunday night farewell, the announced theme is 80s Retro (neon and vintage accessories). Costume participation is completely optional.

entries.title: Where do I check meal times and alternatives to my assigned dinner shift?
entries.text: Full-board meals are included in the buffet and main dining rooms. The buffet provides extended hours including pizza and snacks; exact operating hours appear in the MSC daily ship program. Specialty dining incurs separate charges.

entries.title: How does my dinner shift work? What if I arrive late?
entries.text: Your Cruise Card indicates your assigned main dining room shift and table number. Arrive promptly; kitchen orders allow a 15-minute window before courses advance. If you miss your seating, the buffet provides casual dining alternatives.

entries.title: Can I dine together with friends in other cabins?
entries.text: Immediately after boarding, speak with the restaurant maître d' providing the cabin numbers of your travel group to request table consolidation. The dining team will confirm whether there is room.

entries.title: How do beverage packages work and what are the daily limits?
entries.text: Drink packages are optional. Options include Non-Alcoholic, Easy, and Premium Extra. If booked, all adults sharing a cabin must contract the same package; minors must have the corresponding child package. Alcoholic packages include up to 15 alcoholic beverages per 24-hour cycle (6:00 to 6:00 next day).

entries.title: Is the cabin minibar included in beverage packages?
entries.text: No. Items consumed directly from the in-cabin minibar are billed separately to your account and are not included in standard packages.

entries.title: How do I purchase Wi-Fi internet? Does mobile signal work in Búzios?
entries.text: Satellite internet packages are purchased separately per device and are locked to the specific hardware registered upon activation (cannot be transferred or shared). In Búzios, Brazilian mobile cellular signal may be available depending on carrier and location.

entries.title: Can I use the MSC for Me app and chat without an internet package?
entries.text: Yes. Connect to the ship's internal Wi-Fi network without purchasing internet to use MSC for Me features and internal chat (for guests 16+). Adding "Kriativo" to your display name helps friends find you.

entries.title: How do I settle onboard expenses? Are international cards accepted?
entries.text: Purchases on board are charged to your Cruise Card. Link a physical credit/debit card (including enabled international cards) or settle with a cash deposit at reception. Check currency and activation requirements with your bank prior to boarding.

entries.title: How do I book specialty restaurants on this sailing?
entries.text: Specialty venues such as Kaito Sushi Bar operate separately from full board. MSC lists Butcher’s Cut debuting on MSC Musica in late 2026. Verify operational restaurants and reserve a table directly on board.

entries.title: What should I check regarding travel insurance coverage?
entries.text: Travel insurance is recommended to cover unforeseen cancellations or onboard medical assistance. Request the official policy from Royal Trip and check coverage limits, currencies, deductibles, and deadlines before purchasing.

entries.title: My medication requires refrigeration or special needs. What should I do?
entries.text: Inform Royal Trip in advance via private message so requests can be forwarded to MSC medical staff. Do not rely on the cabin minibar for precise temperature storage. Keep medicines in your carry-on luggage.

entries.title: How does the kids club work? Does staff change diapers or provide meals?
entries.text: MSC offers kids clubs organized by age groups. Children wearing diapers must be accompanied by a guardian during general recreation activities, as youth counselors do not provide diaper changing or meals. Confirm specific services with youth staff on board.

entries.title: Are water, tea, and coffee complimentary? Will we have the Aqua system?
entries.text: Water dispensers, hot water, tea, and drip coffee are available in the buffet restaurant during service hours. The Aqua reusable bottle system availability on MSC Musica should be confirmed with the ship crew.

entries.title: What time must I vacate my cabin on Monday morning?
entries.text: Cabins must be vacated early to prepare for the subsequent sailing. Follow the exact time specified in the onboard disembarkation program delivered to your cabin on the final evening.

entries.title: How do I pack and collect luggage for disembarkation?
entries.text: Follow MSC color-coded luggage tags and instructions provided in your cabin. Leave checked luggage outside your door by the indicated hour on Sunday night. Retrieve luggage in the terminal customs hall in Santos.

entries.title: Should companions join official groups? Whom should I contact?
entries.text: Add travel companions and cabin family members to the official broadcast group to receive event announcements. Contact the cabin lead or our team to request invitation links. For booking/vouchers, message Royal Trip privately.

entries.title: What are the boarding date and times?
entries.text: Boarding is on November 20 (Friday) at the Port of Santos, with a reference check-in window of 9 AM to 3 PM. Disembarkation is on November 23 (Monday), starting at 7 AM. These times are for reference: follow the arrival window and instructions on your booking voucher and MSC's announcements on board.

entries.title: What do I need to have with me at boarding?
entries.text: Bring your printed boarding voucher and your original ID in good condition, with a photo that allows identification. For Brazilian citizens on this domestic itinerary, MSC accepts the RG (Brazilian ID card), CNH (Brazilian driver's license), passport and other civil documents listed in its official rules, and does not require the RG to have been issued less than ten years ago. The digital CNH must be opened in the official app; photos, screenshots and copies, even certified ones, do not replace the document. We also recommend bringing the physical document. For minors, check with Royal Trip which documents and consent forms are required depending on who is traveling with them. Foreign guests must confirm with the agency the documents that apply to their nationality.

entries.title: When can I check in?
entries.text: Royal Trip handles the group's check-in. After the announcement in the WhatsApp group, the person responsible for each cabin should message Júnior/Royal Trip privately to request the official vouchers and luggage labels. Check the details of every passenger and print the documents before boarding.

entries.title: Do I need to be vaccinated to board?
entries.text: Check the current health requirements for your sailing with Royal Trip and MSC. Don't rely on old vaccination or antigen-test rules as current instructions: requirements may change depending on the health situation, the destination and the authorities. Follow the official guidance you receive for your boarding.

entries.title: How do I check my luggage, and when?
entries.text: Dropping off your luggage is the first thing to do when you arrive at the port. If you're driving, luggage drop-off is very close to the parking lot.

entries.title: Is there transportation to the port?
entries.text: Yes! We offer an official round-trip charter bus between Barra Funda (São Paulo), at Rua Tagipuru, near no. 552, and the Port of Santos. Bus 1: meet at 6:00 AM, departure at 6:30 AM (confirmed). Bus 2: meet at 6:40 AM, departure at 7:20 AM, subject to a minimum number of passengers; if the minimum isn't reached, a full refund will be issued via Pix (Brazil's instant payment system). The return from the port on Monday (Nov 23) is scheduled for 10:30 AM. See the charter bus and book your seat.

entries.title: How do I handle parking?
entries.text: You need to book a parking spot in advance to avoid it being full. Details on the Concais parking lot and hotel suggestions are here on the site, in the Transportation & Accommodation section.

entries.title: Who is Royal Trip?
entries.text: Royal Trip is the event's official partner travel agency, with more than 14 years in air and sea travel, plus themed cruises, corporate events and weddings on ships. CNPJ 16.957.402/0001-19.

entries.title: What is the MSC Musica's itinerary?
entries.text: Departure from Santos (SP) on Nov 20, bound for Búzios (RJ), returning to Santos on Nov 23.

entries.title: Can pregnant guests or babies sail on the cruise?
entries.text: MSC does not allow travel if a pregnancy reaches 24 weeks at any point during the cruise. Pregnant guests below that limit must present a medical certificate stating gestational age, expected due date, and confirmation of a low-risk pregnancy and fitness to travel, with the doctor's CRM (Brazilian medical license number), signature and stamp. Let Royal Trip know in advance so they can forward the documents and review your booking. Babies can join this mini-cruise, but they must be listed on the cabin booking; confirm fares and fees with the agency.

entries.title: Will there be a room for playing games?
entries.text: Yes! The Crystal Lounge is the planned venue for Kriativos On Board. We'll confirm the room and hours in the group and in the event schedule. Tables are open and shared on a rotating basis among participants.

entries.title: Which games will be available?
entries.text: The official game library is organized in the Board Game Guru app. You'll find hundreds of modern games from our partners, and Encounter's game teachers will be there to teach you the rules. You can also bring your own games!

entries.title: How does the games app work, and how do I enter the giveaways?
entries.text: We use the official Board Game Guru app (available for Android and iOS). In the app, open the Kriativos On Board page and confirm your early check-in by tapping "Eu vou" ("I'm going"). This step is essential to enter the giveaways of games and exclusive prizes on board! In the app you can also browse the game library, see which game teachers teach each title and register in advance the games you'll bring on board (with direct import from Ludopedia or BoardGameGeek).

entries.title: Can I bring my own games and prototypes?
entries.text: Yes! You can bring as many games as you like, plus prototypes and new releases to play with the community.

entries.title: Can I take games to other areas of the ship?
entries.text: Yes, to any area except the restaurants (the tables are for meals). The game is your responsibility: when you take it out of the room, leave your name and cabin number so it can be checked when you return it.

entries.title: Until what time is the game room open?
entries.text: The idea is to play a lot during the day and at night. The room's hours will be confirmed in the group and in the schedule. On Sunday night, we'll let you know the deadline for returning games and clearing the tables for the final inventory.

entries.title: How does Wi-Fi work, and how do we communicate on board?
entries.text: MSC's satellite internet package is purchased separately for browsing the external internet. When you connect to the ship's internal Wi-Fi network, you can use the MSC for Me app and its free chat. Add "Kriativo" to your profile name or nickname so your friends can find you! During the port call in Búzios, there may be 4G/5G signal from Brazilian carriers, depending on coverage and your location. Check the day of the port call in your booking's official itinerary.

entries.title: Is the safety drill mandatory?
entries.text: Yes. Complete the mandatory procedure MSC indicates for your boarding; the crew will tell you the place, time and steps, including instructions in the app. Watching a video or opening the app alone doesn't fulfill every requirement.

entries.title: How is a board game cruise different from other events?
entries.text: Kriativos On Board combines the love of games with a complete vacation at sea. You enjoy full board, cabin accommodation, the leisure of a luxury ocean liner and a space dedicated to games, according to the event schedule, to play and make lifelong friends.

entries.title: What's included in my booking?
entries.text: Accommodation in your chosen category and full board (breakfast, lunch and dinner), plus water, tea and coffee at the buffet restaurants, subject to availability.

entries.title: Is food unlimited on the ship?
entries.text: Yes. The main restaurants (buffet) serve daily meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner. If you can't make the served dinner time, you can eat at these buffets.

entries.title: How does dinner work on the ship?
entries.text: The main restaurant serves à la carte dinner in pre-assigned sittings, shown on your cruise card, with a starter, main course and dessert. Arrive on time: the 15-minute grace period refers to kitchen orders. If you miss your sitting, check the buffet and pizzeria options; the pizzeria usually runs almost 24 hours. Check the times in MSC's daily schedule.

entries.title: Can I sit at the same dinner table as friends from other cabins?
entries.text: You can ask. Tables for the à la carte dinner are assigned at check-in. To bring family and friends from other cabins to the same table for the cruise, go to the restaurant's maître d' right after boarding on the first day (Friday afternoon) with all the cabin numbers and ask to combine tables. The staff will confirm whether there's still room at dinner.

entries.title: Do I have to buy a drink package?
entries.text: No, it's optional. If someone in the cabin buys a package, the other guests must follow MSC's rules: adults with the same package and children/teens with the Non-Alcoholic package for kids, according to their age group. Babies don't need a package. Confirm with Royal Trip the conditions that apply to your cabin and the deadline to buy.

entries.title: What drink packages are available for adults?
entries.text: Non-Alcoholic, Easy and Premium Extra. Easy and Premium Extra include a maximum of 15 alcoholic drinks per person per day; MSC's daily period runs from 6 AM to 6 AM the next day. Confirm with Royal Trip the prices, discounts, installments and conditions available at the time of purchase.

entries.title: Do I get a minibar in the cabin with the Premium package?
entries.text: All MSC Musica cabins have a minibar, but minibar items are NOT included in any drink package (not even Premium Extra) and are charged separately to your cabin account. Tip: you can pick up canned or bottled drinks at the bars included in your package and keep them in your cabin's minibar to enjoy whenever you like.

entries.title: What does the cabin provide, and what should I pack?
entries.text: Cabins provide bed linen, towels, liquid soap, shampoo, a hair dryer, TV, air conditioning and a safe; check with the agency which amenities your booked category includes. What you MUST bring: toothbrush and toothpaste, hair conditioner, sunscreen and a compatible plug adapter, if needed. Also remember to pack comfortable clothes for game time, smart casual attire for the à la carte dinner (tank tops and flip-flops are not allowed), white clothes for the White Party and themed/neon pieces for the 80s Night!

entries.title: Do I need formal wear for dinner?
entries.text: No. For dinner, wear smart casual attire; the main restaurant doesn't allow tank tops or flip-flops. Check the ship's guidance for each venue and evening.

entries.title: How do I pay for onboard spending? Can I use US dollars?
entries.text: Onboard purchases are charged to the account linked to your cabin card (Cruise Card). Confirm with MSC or at reception which payment methods are accepted to link or settle this account, the currency and whether deposits are possible. If you'll use an international credit card, enable international use and bring the physical card.

entries.title: Is travel insurance mandatory?
entries.text: Insurance is optional and recommended for unexpected events and medical expenses. The approximate price is R$ 112 per person; confirm the policy and terms with Royal Trip before buying.

entries.title: Is there a kids' club or children's activities on the ship?
entries.text: Yes! MSC's Doremi Club offers supervised activities for children and teens by age group. Hours are usually long, around 9 AM to 11 PM, and should be checked in the daily schedule on board. Potty-trained children can stay with the youth staff; children who still wear diapers can use the spaces with their parents or guardians.

entries.title: I take medication that needs refrigeration. What should I do?
entries.text: Let Royal Trip know in advance, through a private channel, so they can forward your request to MSC and confirm the arrangements. Don't count on the cabin minibar keeping the temperature your medication requires, and carry your medication in your hand luggage.

entries.title: What can't I bring on board?
entries.text: MSC prohibits weapons, illegal drugs, flammable materials and heating appliances such as clothes irons. Hair dryers and hair straighteners are allowed. Drones may be carried if stored in the cabin, but using them on board is prohibited. For food, MSC allows commercially packaged dry snacks as an exception; check the full official list and the conditions for special needs.

entries.title: What parties will there be on the ship?
entries.text: We'll have two unforgettable theme nights: the classic White Party (bring something white) and the 80s Night (retro style, accessories and neon colors to celebrate on Sunday night). Themed outfits aren't mandatory, but they make the experience on board even more fun! Check times and venues in the schedule.

entries.title: A 16-deck ocean liner for unforgettable days
entries.text: MSC Musicathe world aboard a cruise ship Day and night, MSC Musica features live music, theater shows, bars and lounges, a casino, spa, and a dedicated kids' area. At the center of it all: an exclusive gaming lounge, available according to the event schedule, for the Kriativos.

entries.title: All-Inclusive Experience
entries.text: Cabin accommodation, full dining, and the entire MSC Musica amenities are all taken care of. Plus, enjoy the private game room according to the event schedule exclusively for KOB attendees.

entries.title: Your gaming lounge
entries.text: Crystal Lounge is the planned venue for KOB gaming sessions. The room still depends on final ship confirmation. Tables operate on an open, rotating basis: please make room for other players once your game concludes. Extensive hours are planned throughout the day and evening. There is no promise of 24h non-stop operation. Respect Sunday's inventory return cutoff time.

entries.title: Welcome kit & schedule
entries.text: The kit includes a lanyard/badge for cabin keys, wristband, commemorative collectible coin, and a sturdy board game tote bag from Fácil Shopping. Pickup is estimated for 16:00/16:30 on day one. The entrance board in the gaming hall will display the daily timetable. Check official channels for any schedule updates.

entries.title: Board Game Guru App
entries.text: Download Board Game Guru (available on iOS and Android) and open the Kriativos On Board event page. Tap ‘I’m going’ to be eligible for raffles. If unable to use the app, contact Encounter staff to request manual registration. Use the app to browse the game catalog, filter titles, and bookmark favorites.

entries.title: Monitors & Finding tables
entries.text: Encounter monitors will help you select games and teach rules. Solo travelers and newcomers can easily connect with friendly groups. You are welcome to bring personal board games and prototypes, within luggage limits. When taking library games outside the lounge, register your name and cabin with the monitor desk.

entries.title: Tournaments & Closing party
entries.text: Check the daily notice board for confirmed tournaments and raffle schedules. Bring your 80s retro outfit for Sunday night's farewell celebration!

Welcome and trip overview
entries.text: We're live. Good evening, Kriativos! Welcome, everyone, to Nerd Kriativa. Let us know if the audio is OK and the video looks good. A warm welcome to you all! We're getting ready to board the next Kriativos On Board over the Black Consciousness Day holiday (November 20–23). You asked for a holiday trip, and here it is. You asked for MSC, and we delivered MSC! I'm here with Júnior from Royal Trip, our longtime partner.

entries.title: Royal Trip and the fourth KOB edition
entries.text: Júnior (Royal Trip): Good evening! For those who've only talked to me on WhatsApp or just paid through the link, I'm Júnior from Royal Trip. That's 14 years as an agency and 4 years of Kriativos On Board. This is our fourth adventure and our first time with MSC, which is big news and a real challenge for us. Our goal is to avoid repeating ships so we get to know different ships and places. This time we're sailing on the MSC Musica, bound for Búzios.

entries.title: Dates, disembarkation and return charter
entries.text: Boarding is on November 20 (Friday, the Black Consciousness Day holiday). Return is on the morning of November 23 (Monday). Disembarkation: once you've had breakfast, it's time to disembark. You need to vacate your cabin early (by around 10 AM) because passengers for the next cruise will be boarding. That's why our return charter bus is scheduled for 10:30 AM.

entries.title: Documents and travel consent for minors
entries.text: What do you need to bring to board? What documents are required? Júnior: Since this is a domestic route (Santos to Búzios), you can use an RG (Brazilian ID card) or a CNH (Brazilian driver's license), digital or physical, as long as it's valid and has a recognizable photo. - Digital CNH: ATTENTION! A screenshot is NOT accepted! If you show the digital version, you must open the official CNH app on the spot, in front of the inspector. If the internet fails or the app goes down, you'll be stuck. So, preferably, bring the PHYSICAL DOCUMENT. - Photocopies: Neither certified copies nor plain photocopies are accepted. - Old RG: For domestic trips, MSC doesn't require the RG to be less than 10 years old, as long as it's in good condition and the photo clearly identifies the holder (it can't be a photo of you as a baby or a 3-year-old). - Minors not traveling with their parents: If you're bringing a nephew or niece, a grandchild or any minor traveling without one or both parents, a travel consent form is mandatory. Júnior provides the correct template to participants. Travel consent for minors depends on who accompanies them. Check your case with Royal Trip.

entries.title: Vouchers, check-in and luggage labels
entries.text: How check-in and vouchers work: Unlike previous years with Costa Cruises, when guests had to complete online check-in themselves, with MSC Royal Trip handles the whole process internally! Júnior will issue and release the vouchers with QR codes and the luggage labels for each cabin. When he announces it in the WhatsApp group, the person responsible for each cabin messages him privately to receive the PDF. Just print it and bring it to the port along with your official ID.

entries.title: Port arrival and boarding queue
entries.text: So our tip is always to get to the port early. If you're coming on the bus, the schedule is perfect. And if you're getting there on your own, try to arrive at the port at 9 AM or before. Why? So you can drop off your luggage and get your boarding number. Boarding works by numbered tickets. When you get your voucher, it'll show a boarding time. Disregard it. Instead, arrive by 9 AM or earlier so you can get your number, and then you'll be among the first to board, and the stress is much lower. Follow the arrival window and instructions on your voucher and from the agency; do not ignore your booking time.

entries.title: Airports and getting to Santos
entries.text: Airports: - Campinas (Viracopos): About 3 hours from Santos by car. Not recommended. - Congonhas: About 40 minutes to 1 hour from Santos, but there are few direct bus times to Santos and it's hard to match them with flights. - Guarulhos (GRU): The best option if you're coming from out of town. It's about 1 hour 40 minutes from Santos, but Viação Cometa runs buses continuously straight to Santos, and even straight to the port. - If you arrive at the Santos bus station, you're only 10 minutes by Uber/taxi from the Concais Terminal.

entries.title: Parking at Concais
entries.text: Parking at the port: Official recommendation: Concais's official parking lot (book in advance at www.concais.com.br). Your car stays inside the port terminal, you get out right where luggage is checked, and on disembarkation your car is right at the door. There are other parking lots in the city, but Concais offers the most security and convenience.

entries.title: Cruise Card, cards and onboard spending
entries.text: Spending and the cabin card (Cruise Card): On board, you don't use cash or bank cards for purchases at the bars, shops or casino. Everything is charged to your cabin card (your cabin key). - You can register an international credit card through the MSC for Me app, at the interactive kiosks or at the ship's reception. - Physical international cards are accepted: Visa, Mastercard and American Express, plus global accounts such as Wise and Nomad (it's best to bring the physical card with a chip, since contactless payment with your phone may fail if there's no signal). - MSC installments: MSC lets you pay onboard spending in installments (over $100 in up to 6 installments; over $300 in up to 10 installments on a credit card). - Free Shop / Duty Free: Open on board with good prices on perfume, drinks and electronics while the ship is sailing in international waters. Confirm currency, accepted cards and instalments with the agency/MSC before relying on these terms.

entries.title: Buffet and cabin availability
entries.text: When you board in the morning or early afternoon: - Cabins won't be ready yet (cleaning goes on until about 1–2 PM, and the announcement is made over the ship's PA system). - Passengers are directed to the main pool deck, where the buffet restaurant is. - You can start eating and drinking right away! There's an open buffet, snacks and a big MSC novelty: a free pizzeria open almost 24 hours, with fresh pasta and pizza made on board every day. 1–2 pm is an estimate: wait for the MSC announcement.

entries.title: Pregnancy
entries.text: Pregnancy: - Strict international maritime rule: anyone more than 24 weeks pregnant (about 5 to 6 months) CANNOT BOARD. - The ship has no medical support for childbirth or neonatal care at sea. Anyone pregnant beyond this limit should contact Royal Trip immediately to replace the guest or request a cancellation. MSC does not allow travel if pregnancy reaches 24 weeks at any point during the cruise.

entries.title: Babies on the booking
entries.text: Babies: - Newborns are allowed on board with MSC, but they MUST be listed on the cabin booking. A lap child cannot board without being registered. - Port fees apply from birth; cabin fares apply from age 2. Confirm baby fares and fees with the agency; age alone does not guarantee free travel.

entries.title: Water, tea, coffee and the Aqua system
entries.text: Water and sustainability: - The buffet restaurant has dispensers with filtered water, tea and coffee, free of charge. - MSC is rolling out the sustainable "Aqua" system, in which guests with a package receive reusable squeeze bottles to refill at dedicated stations. Availability of the Aqua system on this departure must be confirmed.

entries.title: Drinks packages
entries.text: MSC drink packages: 1. Non-alcoholic: Unlimited non-alcoholic drinks (soft drinks, juices, mocktails, water, specialty coffees). 2. Easy: Includes unlimited non-alcoholic drinks and up to 15 alcoholic drinks per person per day (draft beer, wine by the glass, spirits and cocktails selected from the Easy menu). 3. Premium Extra: Covers premium drinks, craft beers and selected higher-priced labels. - Cabin rule: If one adult in the cabin buys a drink package, all other occupants must buy the same package. Check the current MSC rules for limits and cabin occupants.

entries.title: Pay-as-you-go drinks and advance booking
entries.text: And what if you haven't bought one? If you haven't, you register your credit card to your cabin or make a deposit in reais or dollars to leave as credit on the cabin, and you keep spending as usual with the ship key, just like on Costa, and pay at the end. Like, I want to do it in advance because it's worth it, right? The drink package bought in advance is less than half the price. Easy is currently R$ 768 per person, in 12 installments. The non-alcoholic one is R$ 615. Last year, the people buying the R$ 600 package on board were paying R$ 1,300 per person. On board everything is in dollars and the price is completely different, OK? So if you haven't bought yet and want to, you can do it with me up to 20 days before boarding and again pay in 12 installments, no problem. And if you didn't buy the package, can you bring a bottle to fill with water? In theory you can't bring a squeeze bottle, but everyone does. It's not prohibited to bring it on board. They just don't like you going up with your bottle and filling it there. But there are lots of cups right next to it. Nothing stops you from setting the bottle down, filling a cup and pouring it into the bottle. [laughs] A Brazilian workaround, right? There's a little sign there, a bottle with an X: don't fill. But the cup is fine. All with the bottle right beside you. But if the Aqua system comes, that won't end the problem either. Yeah, I think this Aqua system is really cool. So here's the tip for anyone who hasn't booked the package yet: contact Júnior up to 20 days before, pay in 12 installments and avoid the headache. How much would each installment be? Math isn't my thing. No, 12 on 600 is about R$ 40, more or less, for the non-alcoholic one, and a bit over 50 for Easy. Right. So it's worth it, right? That way you don't go through that either. Prices and deadlines quoted belong to the presentation. Confirm the current offer with Royal Trip.

entries.title: Restaurants and dinner sittings
entries.text: Included restaurants: - Pool buffet: Open self-service for breakfast, lunch, afternoon snack, dinner and late night (pizzeria open almost 24 hours). - Main restaurant (à la carte): Dinner with full table service (starter, main course and dessert, and you can order dishes again). - Fixed time and table: Shown on your cabin card (1st sitting ~7:15 PM; 2nd sitting ~9:30 PM). Your actual sitting is on the cruise card; the grace period refers to kitchen orders.

entries.title: Dinner with friends in other cabins
entries.text: So, let's say I'm going with my wife, my sister and her husband, and my brother-in-law with my nephew. We're in several cabins. What's assigned here is per cabin. If you want to sit together at dinner, on the very first day, when you board, you need to stop by reception and ask where the maître d' is. They'll tell you where the maître d' will be and at what time. Then one person from each cabin goes to the maître d' and says: "We're a group and we want to sit together." Then he puts you together at the same dinner table. It has to be done on the first day. Once the first dinner has passed, forget it: you'll stay where you are. The à la carte restaurant is really nice for the experience Karen mentioned. The dishes are very refined and really tasty. You sit down, the waiter comes, hands you the menu, you choose a starter, main course and dessert, and you can order again. At first I didn't get it; I didn't like it, it took a while, the portion was small. We also affectionately call the self-service the cafeteria. The cafeteria upstairs will be open: go up and you can eat again. There'll be snacks going around too. The pizzeria will be open. So don't worry about food. That's it. And if you really liked a dish, no problem, they're serving you right there and you can order it again, but ideally you order everything up front, because they have everything scheduled in the kitchen. So, like: I want a starter, two desserts and the main course, and I want both desserts, but order them up front, because that way they bring everything as scheduled, OK? Yes. So,

entries.title: Dinner time and late arrival
entries.text: remembering the schedule, there's the time you'll have dinner. It's either 7:15 PM or 9:30 PM. If you arrive more than 15 minutes late for the time on your card, you can't go in for dinner anymore. You'll have to eat at the cafeteria. At the cafeteria. Why? Because the waiter waits those 15 minutes, everyone sits down, he comes, takes everyone's order, and then the kitchen downstairs starts preparing and sending out the dishes. So if you arrive late, you delay the whole table, because when the waiter serves, he serves the starter to everyone. Until everyone finishes eating, he doesn't clear and serve the next course. So if you arrive half an hour late, everyone else's food will be almost arriving and your order will just be going in. That's why you can't go in. That's it. Dinner and meals explained. And now the minibar, right? The minibar. The ships have a minibar. MSC usually keeps it stocked. Check the sitting and time on your Cruise Card and confirm instructions with the onboard crew.

entries.title: Travel insurance and medical expenses
entries.text: Health / travel insurance: - It isn't mandatory, but it's highly recommended. The onboard medical center charges in dollars at very high international rates (just the initial consultation is around USD 50, and simple procedures such as dressings or treatment can reach USD 800–USD 1,000 / R$ 5,000+). - Travel insurance with MSC's official insurer costs R$ 112 per person and provides medical coverage of US$ 40,000 (or R$ 40,000), plus coverage for luggage damage and cancellation. - Exclusive condition for Kriativos: the insurer kept the extended coverage for 29 cancellation reasons even if purchased later (up to 20 days before boarding). The spoken coverage amount and currency are ambiguous. Check the current policy and offer with Royal Trip.

entries.title: Children and the kids club
entries.text: MSC kids' facilities: - MSC's official kids club is called Doremi Club, divided by age group (Doremi Kids from 6 to 11, Teens from 11 to 17). - Long daily hours (usually 9 AM to 11 PM). - Diaper rule: To stay with the youth staff without a parent, the child must already be potty-trained. Children who wear diapers can play in the space only when accompanied by their parents or guardians. The ship's staff don't change diapers or provide meals at the kids club. Confirm kids-club conditions with the crew; services such as Baby Care have separate rules.

entries.title: Luggage
entries.text: Luggage rules: - MSC's formal limit: up to 3 suitcases per passenger (up to 90 kg in total). There are no weighing scales at the Port of Santos. The spoken allowance differs from MSC. Per person: two suitcases of up to 23 kg each and two pieces of hand luggage of up to 10 kg each. Per cabin: no more than 100 kg and/or eight pieces. Check dimensions and other conditions in the guide.

entries.title: Allowed and prohibited luggage items
entries.text: What to bring and what's prohibited: - Expressly prohibited: clothes irons (stopped on the spot at the X-ray scanner), weapons, illegal substances, drones. Use the current MSC list: hairdryers and straighteners are allowed; carrying a drone differs from using it onboard.

entries.title: What your cabin provides
entries.text: The cabin has a hair dryer, we forgot to mention it. All the cabins are super comfortable, and they have a private bathroom, liquid soap, towels and shampoo. Soap, shampoo. Soap and shampoo. There's no toothpaste or conditioner, so you need to bring those. There's bed linen and towels, a safe, the minibar, a TV, air conditioning and a small hair dryer, either on a holder in the bathroom or in the vanity drawer. As for the minibar, just use it, like, put your own things in it; don't take things out. Since MSC hands out cans, their system is different from Costa's: you can go to the bar and say, I want two Cokes. You take them, bring them to the cabin and put them there. Late at night you have your water, your Coke, without having to worry about restocking it later.

entries.title: Official group and final reminders
entries.text: Add all your cabin companions and family members to the event's official WhatsApp group. Urgent notices and onboard instructions are sent while messaging is temporarily locked, so everyone reads them. There's news coming with the official Jogos & Vestes T-shirts and new partnerships on the horizon. See you on board the MSC Musica on November 20!
